name: Miri famine-relief wheel spinning
description: At Miri near Ahmednagar, women spun yarn on loaned wheels in a famine-relief project recorded in 1921.

impact.note: One relief project using the long-established spinning wheel in a single village, with no lasting change or successors known.

date.basis: Date for the cited specific instance, not an invention or global priority date.

events.statement: At Miri near Ahmednagar, women spun yarn on loaned wheels in a famine-relief project recorded in 1921.

evidence.locator: Spinning as Famine Relief, Young India 11 May 1921
evidence.supports: The contemporary account describes work begun in January, wheels lent because people could not afford them, local wheel-making and reported rates.

events.caveats: The organizer’s account is one project report, not independent evidence for regional prevalence, net wages or an end to famine; spinning wheels and textiles are much older.
